title: Mate in two: checks first
line: A check that leaves one reply, then mate.

steps.text: No check mates at once here. So look for a check that leaves the king a single reply, then a mate after that reply.
Check with the rook on the back rank. The king has one square to go to.

wrong.c4g8: The king takes the queen. Nothing guards g8 yet.

steps.hint: The rook goes up the open file.
steps.after: Forced: the king had only one square.

steps.text: Now the rook guards g8. Mate with the queen.
steps.hint: The queen goes along the diagonal to the square beside the king.
steps.after: Checkmate. The rook guards the queen, and the king's own pieces take its last squares.

steps.text: Find both moves yourself. First, the check that leaves one reply.

wrong.h1h6: The king steps away to g7 or g8, and there is no mate.

steps.hint: Your rook on the open edge file guards a pawn capture next to the king.
steps.after: The king cannot take the queen, because the rook guards her. Its only square is g8.

steps.hint: The queen takes on the edge, still guarded by the rook.

steps.text: One more. Check first, then mate.

wrong.h1h8: The king takes the queen. Nothing guards that corner.

steps.hint: The knight guards one square beside the king.
steps.after: The king's only square was f8.

steps.hint: The queen moves one square along the edge to the corner.
steps.after: Checkmate. The king is too far away to take the queen, the knight covers f7, and Black's own pieces block the rest.

summary: When no check mates at once, find a check that leaves one reply, and look for the mate after it.
